This crusader lord ruled Antioch and Transjordan by right of marriage, and once tortured the Latin Patriarch of Antioch over unpaid funds before raiding Byzantine Cyprus — who was he?
Raynald of Châtillon: Crusader and military leader (1125–1187)
The longest-serving U.S. secretary of defense, this Cold War-era Pentagon chief championed systems analysis and escalated American involvement in the Vietnam War — who was he?
Robert McNamara: American businessman and government official (1916–2009)
This politician resigned as Kyrgyzstan's acting president in November 2020 just so he could run in — and win — the 2021 election that made him the country's sixth president. Who is he?
Sadyr Japarov: President of Kyrgyzstan since 2021. Japarov returned to Kyrgyzstan in 2017, where he was arrested and sentenced to an 11 year prison term due to his prior illegal political activities.

This early 20th-century youth movement emphasizes outdoor skills like camping and woodcraft, uses a uniform designed to hide social class differences, and awards merit badges bearing a fleur-de-lis. What movement is it?
Scouting: Youth movement. Scouting or the Scout Movement is a youth movement which became popularly established in the first decade of the 20th century.
One of Noah's sons in Genesis, this biblical figure is considered an ancestor of Abraham and lent his name to the term for a group of West Asian peoples — who is he?
Shem: Biblical figure, son of Noah. Shem (Hebrew: שֵׁם Šēm; Arabic: سَام, romanized: Sām) is one of the sons of Noah in the Bible (Genesis 5–11 and 1 Chronicles 1:4).
This left-wing ideology is defined by social ownership of the means of production — public, cooperative, or employee-held — rather than private ownership. What is it?
Socialism: Political philosophy emphasising social ownership of production.
Nicknamed the 'Tiger King' for his ferocity, this 29th monarch of the Ayutthaya Kingdom is credited with devising the fundamental techniques of Muay Thai — who is he?
Known by a name meaning 'behind the pool' after the palace where he resided, this monarch ruled the Ayutthaya Kingdom from 1709 to 1733 as the third ruler of the Ban Phlu Luang dynasty — who is he?
Thai Sa: King of Ayutthaya. The name "Thai Sa" (lit. "behind the pool") refers to the Banyongrattanat Palace, which was located by a pool where he often resided.

Japan's first socialist premier in nearly half a century, this 1990s prime minister is best remembered for an official statement apologizing for his country's past colonial wars on the 50th anniversary of WWII's end. Who was he?
Tomiichi Murayama: Prime Minister of Japan from 1994 to 1996.
This Russian dissident and writer founded and chaired the Democratic Union party and sat on the editorial board of The New Times before her death in 2014 — who is she?
Controlled until 2023 by Yevgeny Prigozhin, this Russian state-funded private military company first emerged fighting in the Donbas war — which group?
Wagner Group: Russian private military company. The Wagner Group has used infrastructure of the Russian Armed Forces.
Dying just 31 days into office in 1841, this ninth U.S. president holds the record for shortest term ever served — who is he?
William Henry Harrison: President of the United States in 1841.
Cairo-born and a founding member of Fatah, he chaired the PLO from 1969 until his death in 2004 — which Palestinian leader?
Yasser Arafat: President of Palestine from 1989 to 2004.
Elected mayor of Guatemala City six times, this president's crowning achievement was the 1996 peace accord that ended his country's 36-year civil war — who was he?
Who among these was born first?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four. Richards graduated from Westford Academy (second oldest secondary school in Massachusetts) in 1862.
Which of these four began earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
John Cockcroft is a physicist. Ernest Rutherford accepted Cockcroft as a research student in the Cavendish Laboratory, and Cockcroft completed his doctorate under Rutherford's supervision in 1928.
Who among these is a chemist?
Linus Pauling is a chemist. Linus Carl Pauling ( PAW-ling; February 28, 1901 – August 19, 1994) was an American chemist and peace activist.
What is the atomic number of Nobelium?
Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
In what year was Katherine Johnson born?
Katherine Johnson: The space agency noted her "historical role as one of the first African-American women to work as a NASA scientist".
In what year was Ratan Tata born?
Ratan Tata: Ratan Naval Tata (28 December 1937 – 9 October 2024) was an Indian industrialist and philanthropist.
In what year was Ursula von der Leyen born?
Ursula von der Leyen: Von der Leyen was born and raised in Brussels, Belgium, to German parents.
In what year did Jean Piaget die?
Jean Piaget: Jean William Fritz Piaget (9 August 1896 – 16 September 1980) was a Swiss psychologist known for his work on child development.
In what year did Doc Holliday die?
Doc Holliday: Holliday is best known for his role in the events surrounding and his participation in the gunfight at the O.K.
In what year was Radon discovered?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
In what year was Adenosine triphosphate discovered?
Adenosine triphosphate: When consumed in a metabolic process, ATP converts either to adenosine diphosphate (ADP) or to adenosine monophosphate (AMP).
Mil Mi-26: Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant. The Mil Mi-26 (Russian: Миль Ми-26, NATO reporting name: Halo) is a Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.
Which country is Artemy Lebedev from?
Artemy Lebedev: Russia. Artemy Andreyevich Lebedev (Russian: Артемий Андреевич Лебедев; born 13 February 1975) is a Russian designer, entrepreneur and Internet personality.
Who is credited with discovering Rhodium?
Rhodium: William Hyde Wollaston. Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Who is credited with discovering Ibuprofen?
Ibuprofen: Stewart Adams. Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that is used to relieve pain, fever, and inflammation.
Who is credited with discovering Carbon?
Carbon: Antoine Lavoisier. Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
Drugs that meddle with this neurotransmitter can do everything from paralyze to cause convulsions, since it's the signal motor neurons use to activate muscles. What is it?
Acetylcholine (ACh) is an organic compound that functions in the brain and body of many types of animals (including humans) as a neurotransmitter.
This genus of more than 650 flowering succulent species includes a 'true' member cultivated worldwide as the standard source for a soothing pharmaceutical gel — what's the genus?
Aloe (also written Alo) is a genus containing over 650 species of flowering succulent plants.
A spinoff of The Originals set within a broader vampire-fiction universe, this CW series follows a teenage witch navigating her supernatural legacy. What show is it?
Anteater are the four extant mammal species in the suborder Vermilingua (meaning 'worm tongue'), commonly known for eating ants and termites.
About a third of the several hundred mold species in this genus have a sexual reproductive stage, and some cause infections while others hold commercial value — which genus?
Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Six carbons in a flat hexagonal ring, each wearing a single hydrogen — this textbook aromatic hydrocarbon has the formula C6H6 — what is it?
Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6.
With the formula B(OH)3 and found in nature as the mineral sassolite, this weak, water-soluble compound of boron serves as an antiseptic, insecticide, and flame retardant — which acid?
Boric acid is a compound of boron, oxygen, and hydrogen with formula B(OH)3.

Native to the Philippines and nearby Southeast Asia, this small sour citrus fruit — a natural hybrid of kumquat and mandarin — flavors everything from marinades to beverages in Filipino cooking — which fruit?
Calamansi (Citrus microcarpa), also known as calamondin, Philippine lime, or Philippine lemon, is a citrus hybrid cultivated predominantly in the Philippines.
Separated from the small intestine by the ileocecal valve, this pouch — whose Latin root means 'blind' — kicks off the large intestine and, in herbivores, helps ferment cellulose. What is it?
Cecum (plural ceca or) is a pouch within the peritoneum that is considered to be the beginning of the large intestine.
This roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle, generated within an organism but tuned by cues like daylight, is regulated by an internal biological clock — what is it called?
Circadian rhythm is a natural oscillation that repeats roughly every 24 hours.
Entering service with Strategic Air Command in 1960, this four-engine, delta-wing supersonic bomber was the first in the world capable of Mach 2 — name the aircraft?

Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight. To achieve the high speeds desired, Convair chose a delta wing design used by contemporary interceptors such as the Convair F-102.
Nearly every genus in this taxonomic family of armadillos is extinct, except for one genus that still includes eight living species today. Name the family?
Dasypodidae is a family of mostly extinct genera of armadillos.
Found in nighttime cold remedies like NyQuil and paired with vitamin B6 for pregnancy-related nausea, this antihistamine is an inverse agonist at the H1 receptor — which drug?
Doxylamine is an antihistamine medication used to treat insomnia and allergies, and - in combination with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) - to treat morning sickness in pregnant women.

These ductless glands throughout the body secrete their products directly into the bloodstream rather than through a duct — together with the pineal, pituitary, thyroid, and others, what are they called?
Endocrine gland is a network of glands and organs located throughout the body.
What is the scientific term for the solid waste material left after digestion, discharged through the anus, and sometimes reused as fertilizer, fuel, or building material?
Feces (also faeces or fces or poop) are the solid or semi-solid remains of food that was not digested in the small intestine, and has been broken down by bacteria in the large intestine.
Alongside co-founding a file-sharing site, this Swedish entrepreneur also started an internet service provider and web-hosting firm called PRQ — who is he?
Fredrik Neij (born 27 April 1978), alias TiAMO, is the co-founder of The Pirate Bay, and the Swedish Internet service provider and web hosting company PRQ.
Built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, this tripeptide is the most abundant low-molecular-mass thiol in most cells and a key antioxidant guarding against free radicals — what is it?
Glutathione (GSH) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.

Also called the harlequin or multicoloured Asian type, this exceptionally variable insect established itself across Africa and South America after being introduced beyond its native Asia — what species?
Harmonia axyridis is a lady beetle or ladybird species that is most commonly known as the harlequin, Asian, or multicoloured Asian lady beetle.

This broad academic category studies human society, culture, and its fundamental questions — during the Renaissance, the term specifically meant the study of classical literature and language as a secular alternative to religious studies. Name the category?
Humanities are academic disciplines that study aspects of human society and culture, including certain fundamental questions asked by humans.

According to Alfred Adler, this persistent psychological feeling of being deficient compared to others — often rooted in childhood upbringing or social status — can drive a person to overcompensate. Name the concept?
Inferiority complex is a consistent feeling of inadequacy, often resulting in the belief that one is in some way deficient, or inferior, to others.
This American businessman and chemist owned the Los Angeles Lakers through their 'Showtime' era of the 1980s, winning 10 league championships as majority owner. Who is he?
Jerry Buss (January 27, 1933 - February 18, 2013) was an American businessman, investor, chemist, and philanthropist.
Found from Africa to the Americas, this family of 118 bird species has big heads and sharp bills, and though most picture them by rivers, many actually live deep in forests — what are they?
Kingfisher are a family, the Alcedinidae, of small to medium-sized, brightly coloured birds in the order Coraciiformes.
This German-born American businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, launching his San Francisco firm in 1853 — who is he?
Levi Strauss (STROWSS; born Lb Strau,; February 26, 1829 - September 26, 1902) was a German-born American businessman who founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans.
Over a 55-year career this American botanist bred more than 800 plant varieties, from the Shasta daisy to the Santa Rosa plum and a spineless cactus for cattle — who was he?

Luther Burbank (March 7, 1849 - April 11, 1926) was an American botanist, horticulturist, and pioneer in agricultural science who developed more than 800 strains and varieties of plants over his 55-year career.
Number theory, algebra, geometry, analysis and set theory are all branches of this field, which leans on logical reasoning and proof to study abstract concepts — what is it?
Mathematics is a field of knowledge concerned with abstract concepts such as numbers, geometric shapes, sets, functions, and probabilities.
This Soviet tandem-seat helicopter was built purely for anti-armor attack missions, carrying no secondary transport capacity unlike the gunship it succeeded — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.

In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature properly and never develop into healthy cells, early on there are often no symptoms, though it can progress into acute leukemia. Name the condition?
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is one of a group of cancers in which blood cells in the bone marrow do not mature, and as a result, do not develop into healthy blood cells.

Jointly operated by the U.S. Air Force and NASA in the 1960s, this rocket-powered experimental aircraft set speed and altitude records, once reaching Mach 6.7 and crossing into the edge of outer space — name this aircraft?

North American X-15 is a hypersonic rocket-powered aircraft formerly operated by the United States Air Force and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) as part of the X-plane series of experimental aircraft.
Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the cycle, this event sees an ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg ready to be fertilized. What's the term?
Ovulation is an important part of the menstrual cycle in female vertebrates where the egg cells are released from the ovaries as part of the ovarian cycle.
This aromatic herb is a natural hybrid between watermint and spearmint, native to Europe and the Middle East but now cultivated worldwide — what plant is it?
Peppermint (Mentha piperita) is a hybrid species of mint, a cross between watermint and spearmint.

This roundworm is one of the most common intestinal parasites in humans, causing a condition sometimes called oxyuriasis after the family it belongs to, and has also been found in bonnet macaques — what's the parasite?
Pinworm (parasite) (species Enterobius vermicularis), also known as threadworm (in the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand) or seatworm, is a parasitic worm.

This male sexual dysfunction occurs when orgasm happens very soon after minimal sexual stimulation, with medical experts generally setting the threshold at around one minute — what's this condition called?

Premature ejaculation (PE) is a male sexual dysfunction that occurs when a male expels semen (and most likely experiences orgasm) soon after beginning sexual activity, and with minimal penile stimulation.
Element 88 on the periodic table, this silvery-white alkaline earth metal turns black when exposed to air and glows via radioluminescence as it radioactively decays — which element?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
This big, sociable black corvid is told apart from its relatives by a bare, whitish patch on its face, and it nests in noisy treetop colonies near farms and villages — which bird is it?
Rook (bird) (Corvus frugilegus) is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds.

These colorful predatory marine animals — single polyps usually anchored by their base — are named after a terrestrial flower and, unlike their jellyfish relatives, skip the medusa stage entirely; what are they?
Sea anemone (-) are a group of predatory marine invertebrate animals constituting the order Actiniaria.
This group of nocturnal Southeast Asian primates ranges from Yunnan province in China down to the island of Java, with a pygmy relative recently reclassified into its own genus — what are they?
Slow loris are a group of several species of nocturnal strepsirrhine primates that make up the genus Nycticebus.
Innervated by the accessory nerve, which of the body's largest and most superficial neck structures rotates the head to the opposite side and flexes the neck?
Sternocleidomastoid muscle is one of the largest and most superficial cervical muscles.

A carnivorous marsupial formerly found across mainland Australia but now confined to Tasmania, this animal became the world's largest carnivorous marsupial after the thylacine's extinction in 1936. What is this fierce creature?
Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii; palawa kani: purinina) is a carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

Sitting at the organizational level between individual cells and a full organ, this biological term for a functional grouping of similar cells derives from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology) is an assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix from the same embryonic origin that together carry out a specific function.
A physician before politics, this German served as Angela Merkel's defence minister and in 2019 became President of the European Commission — who is she?
Ursula von der Leyen (ne Albrecht; born 8 October 1958) is a German politician and physician who has served as President of the European Commission since 2019.
This small insect-eating songbird breeds across most of Europe and Asia, migrates to Africa in winter, and has a black-backed form that predominates in Britain and Ireland — what is it?
White wagtail (Motacilla alba) is a small passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which also includes pipits and longclaws.
The only living member of its entire mammalian order, this nocturnal African burrower uses its long snout and powerful claws to dig ants and termites out of their mounds — what animal is it?
Aardvark: Burrowing mammal native to Africa.
While bacteria and some plants may be biologically immortal, this universal process in humans slows reaction time even as knowledge tends to grow — what is it called?
Ageing: Biological process of getting older.
Though commonly called a nut, this tree's fruit is technically a drupe with a hard shell surrounding an edible seed, closely related to the peach — which food is it?
Almond: Species of nut. The fruit of the almond is a drupe, consisting of an outer hull and a hard shell with the seed, which is not a true nut.
This Manchester physicist shared the 2010 Nobel Prize for his work on graphene — and is the only person to also hold an Ig Nobel, won for levitating a frog with magnetism. Who is he?
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?
One of the oldest of the natural sciences, it leans on math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything from comets to quasars beyond Earth's atmosphere — what field is this?
Astronomy: Scientific study of celestial objects.
The most common type of skin cancer, this slow-growing tumor is sometimes called a 'rodent ulcer' and rarely spreads beyond its original site — what is it?
Basal-cell carcinoma: Most common type of skin cancer. Basal-cell carcinoma (BCC), also known as basal-cell cancer, basalioma, or rodent ulcer, is the most common type of skin cancer.
This field covers physiological traits like fingerprints and iris patterns, plus behavioral ones like typing rhythm and gait, all used to identify people — what is it called?
Biometrics: Metrics related to human characteristics.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Found across North America (and one Siberian species in Asia), these small striped squirrels stash food in their cheek pouches to store for winter — what are they?
This spore-forming, rod-shaped bacterium produces the most potent toxin known to science, causing a severe paralytic illness often linked to bulging canned food — what's its name?
Clostridium botulinum: Species of endospore forming bacterium.

This grayish-brown, wart-skinned amphibian (scientific name Bufo bufo) is found across most of Europe, hides by day, and hunts invertebrates at dusk, moving with a slow, ungainly walk or short jumps — which species?
Common toad: Species of amphibian. It belongs to a group of closely related species descended from a common ancestral line of toads and forming a species complex.
Surprisingly, the closest living relatives of birds are a clan of semiaquatic predators that includes alligators, caimans, and the long-snouted gharial. What is this reptile order?
Crocodilia: Order of reptiles. The teeth are conical and peg-like, and the bite is powerful.
This Manhattan Project physicist later led the Federation of American Scientists and is best remembered for his 1959 Senate testimony opposing Lewis Strauss's Commerce nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill: American nuclear physicist (1919–2008)
Named for the unique double-beamed bones under its tail, this long-necked Jurassic giant is one of the most common fossils found in North America's Morrison Formation. What dinosaur is it?
Diplodocus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs (fossil)
Starting life bilaterally symmetrical as larvae but growing into five-pointed radial adults, this animal phylum includes starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers — what is it called?
Echinoderm: Marine phylum of animals often with radial symmetries.
Often triggered by contaminated food, NSAIDs, or autoimmune conditions like coeliac disease, which medical term describes inflammation of the small intestine?
Enteritis: Inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.

With a wingspan reaching 188 centimeters and distinctive ear tufts atop mottled blackish-and-tawny plumage, this raptor is one of the largest of its nocturnal kind, ranging widely across Europe and Asia — what bird is it?
Eurasian eagle-owl: Species of owl. The Eurasian eagle-owl (Bubo bubo) is a species of eagle-owl, a type of bird that resides much over Eurasia.

An annual legume with leaves of three small leaflets, this semiarid crop has flavored dishes of the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — yet there's little clinical proof it works as the supplement people often take. What is it?
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.

This digestive disorder involves weak stomach muscle contractions that delay how quickly food empties into the intestine, often linked to nerve damage from uncontrolled diabetes — what's the condition called?
Gastroparesis: Medical condition. The opposite of this, where stomach contents exit quickly into the duodenum, is called dumping syndrome.
As the single largest muscle in the human body, this hip extensor gives the buttocks their shape and is a key reason humans can stand upright, unlike other primates — what is it?
Gluteus maximus: Largest and most superficial of the three gluteal muscles.
Breeders prefer to call it a 'cavy,' and despite its name it hails from the Andes rather than West Africa and isn't related to swine at all — which Andean rodent is it?
Guinea pig: Domesticated rodent from South America.
Comprising cicadas, aphids, bed bugs, and more than 80,000 other species with piercing-sucking mouthparts, which insect order is nicknamed the 'true bugs'?
Hemiptera: Order of insects often called true bugs.
First published as a Latin anagram in 1676 by a British physicist, this principle states that the force needed to stretch a spring scales linearly with its extension — which law?
Hooke's law: Force needed to pull a spring grows linearly with distance.

Affecting roughly one in 250 baby boys, this is the second most common birth defect of the male reproductive system, in which a key opening doesn't form in its usual place — what is this condition called?
Hypospadias: Malformation in which the urethral opening is misplaced.
Named after the Greek word for rainbow because its compounds show so many colors, this brittle silvery-white metal is the second-densest element found in nature — what is it?
Iridium: Chemical element with atomic number 77 (Ir)
Built from an umbrella-shaped bell of mesoglea that pulses to swim, this Cnidarian trails stinging tentacles and is the medusa phase of its complex life cycle — what is it?
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this bumpy-skinned citrus fruit is prized in regional cooking for its intensely fragrant leaves and rind, and its oil is used in perfumery — which fruit?
Kaffir lime: Citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia. Citrus hystrix, called the kaffir lime, Thai lime or makrut lime, (US:, UK:) is a citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia.
Making up 2 to 8 percent of milk by mass, this disaccharide combines galactose and glucose and takes its name from the Latin word for milk — what is it?
Lactose: Carbohydrate. Lactose is a disaccharide composed of galactose and glucose and has the molecular formula C12H22O11.
Also sold as Xylocaine, this amino-amide local anesthetic numbs in minutes and doubles as a treatment for dangerous ventricular heart rhythms — what is it?
Lidocaine: Local anesthetic. Lidocaine, also known as lignocaine and sold under the brand name Xylocaine among others, is a local anesthetic of the amino amide type.

Credited as a 'Father of Cinematography,' this French artist filmed the Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888 — then vanished without a trace two years later, and his work never shaped commercial cinema. Who was he?
Louis Le Prince: French motion-picture pioneer (1841–1890s)
Distinguished from living elephants by spirally twisted tusks and a thick coat of fur for cold climates, this extinct genus survived from the late Miocene until roughly 4,000 years ago — what was it?
Mammoth: Extinct genus of mammals. The oldest mammoth representative, Mammuthus subplanifrons, appeared around 6 million years ago during the late Miocene in southern and Eastern Africa.
Home to the heart, esophagus, trachea, thymus, and central chest lymph nodes, this compartment of the thoracic cavity sits between the lungs — what's it called?
Mediastinum: Central part of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum (from Medieval Latin: mediastinus, lit. 'midway';pl.: mediastina) is the central compartment of the thoracic cavity.
Son of a U.S. vice president, this young art collector vanished in 1961 during an expedition into New Guinea's Asmat region, with some accounts claiming he was killed by local tribesmen — who was he?
Michael Rockefeller: American anthropologist and art collector (1938–1961)
Named in 1883 by a German anthropologist who wrongly believed it was most common among his patients, this bluish congenital birthmark usually fades by puberty — what is it?
Mongolian spot: Type of birthmark. It normally disappears three to five years after birth and almost always by puberty.

When light from distant objects focuses in front of the retina rather than on it, far-away things blur while close ones stay sharp — and spending more time outdoors as a child seems to lower the risk. What's this refractive error?
Myopia: Inability to focus on distant objects.
This small sauropod dinosaur had a wide muzzle packed with more than 500 teeth that were replaced roughly every two weeks — what genus is it?
Native to East Africa and known in some places as 'lady's fingers,' this mallow-family plant is prized for its edible green (sometimes red) seed pods — what is it?

Produced in the hypothalamus and nicknamed for its role in love and social bonding, this peptide hormone also doubles as a pharmaceutical that speeds up childbirth by triggering uterine contractions — what is it?
Oxytocin: Peptide hormone and neuropeptide. Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
Prized wood from this fruit tree's genus, Pyrus, is a favorite material for making high-quality woodwind instruments, and China grows about three-quarters of the world's crop — which fruit?
Pear: Edible fruits from the genus Pyrus.

Combining textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly field traces its classical roots to the libraries of Pergamum and Alexandria in the 4th century BC — what is it?
Philology: Study of language in historical sources.
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.
Known by the E number E211, this white crystalline salt of benzoic acid is a widely used food preservative and pickling agent — what is it?
Sodium benzoate: Common food preservative. It appears as a white crystalline chemical with the formula C6H5COONa.
A luminous ball of plasma held together by its own gravity, the closest example to Earth is the Sun — what celestial object is this?
Star: Large self-illuminated object in space.
Despite the naming confusion with true yams, this starchy tuberous root actually belongs to the morning glory family and hails from tropical Ecuador — which crop?

Formerly named France Télécom, this French telecommunications giant's current brand traces back to a UK mobile operator acquired by Hutchison Whampoa in 1994 — what is it called today?
Orange Group: French multinational telecommunications corporation.
Operating both Lidl and Kaufland, this family-owned German retailer posted 185.6 billion euros in revenue in fiscal 2025, making it Europe's largest retailer — which company?
Schwarz Group: German retailer conglomerate. The Schwarz Group (German: Schwarz Gruppe) is a German multinational retailer that operates stores under the Lidl and Kaufland brands.
Headquartered jointly in Lowell, Massachusetts, and Weston, Florida, this company provides workforce and human resource management software — which one?
UKG: American software company. UKG is an American multinational technology company with dual headquarters in Lowell, Massachusetts, and Weston, Florida.
